questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Mary writes computer programs that generate report cards for schools. She includes comments in her programs. She chooses a compiler as an appropriate language translator.

(i) Identify the occupation that best describes Mary's activity. Give reasons for your choice. (2 marks)

(ii) Briefly explain the importance of comments in Mary's programs. (2 marks)

(iii) Mary wants her programs to output "PASSED" for students with averages of 10 and above and "FAILED" for averages below 10. State the programming construct that Mary should use to achieve this. How does this construct work in general? (3 marks)

(iv) Briefly state the function of the compiler used by Mary. (2 marks)

(v) State a different language translator type that Mary could have used. Explain why you think she preferred a compiler. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Occupation (2 marks).** Mary is a **computer programmer** (software developer). Reason: she writes, tests and maintains computer programs in a programming language, which is exactly the work of a programmer (a systems analyst designs systems, a database administrator manages databases).

**(ii) Comments (2 marks).** A comment is explanatory text that the compiler ignores. Comments document the program: they explain what each part does, so that Mary or another programmer can understand, debug, maintain and modify the program later, without affecting how it runs.

**(iii) Construct (3 marks).** She should use a **selection (decision or conditional) construct**, the IF ... THEN ... ELSE statement:

```text
IF average >= 10 THEN
    PRINT "PASSED"
ELSE
    PRINT "FAILED"
END IF
```

How it works: the condition (average >= 10) is evaluated first and is either true or false. If it is true, only the statements of the THEN part are executed; if it is false, only the statements of the ELSE part are executed, and then the program continues after the construct. So exactly one of the two branches is carried out.

**(iv) Function of the compiler (2 marks).** The compiler translates the whole source program, written in a high-level language, into machine code (object code) in one go, and reports all the syntax errors it finds; if there are none it produces an executable program that the computer can run directly.

**(v) Another translator and the reason (3 marks).** Another type of language translator is the **interpreter** (an assembler is used for assembly language). Mary preferred a compiler because the compiled program is translated only once and then runs much faster, which suits report cards processed for many students; the executable can be given to schools without giving away the source code; and the translator does not have to be present each time the program runs, whereas an interpreter translates and runs the program line by line every time it is used.

(b) (i) Briefly explain the difference between batch processing and real-time processing. (4 marks)

(ii) Copy and complete Table 2, with the following:

*Air travel seat reservation booking system, payroll generating system, electric bill generating system, stock exchange market decision system.* (4 marks)

| Batch processing system | Real-time processing system |

| | |
| | |

questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Difference (4 marks).** In **batch processing** the data are collected and stored over a period and then processed together as one batch, at a scheduled time and usually without user interaction; the results are not needed immediately (for example monthly payroll). In **real-time processing** each input is processed immediately, as soon as it is entered, and the system responds within a very short time so that the output can influence the next action or decision; the data are always up to date.

**(ii) Table 2 (4 marks, 1 per system).**

| Batch processing system | Real-time processing system |
|---|---|
| Payroll generating system | Air travel seat reservation booking system |
| Electric bill generating system | Stock exchange market decision system |

Reasons: payrolls and electricity bills are produced for all employees or customers together at the end of a period, so they can wait; seat bookings and stock exchange decisions must be processed at once, because a seat or a share price may change a moment later.
